citation.authors: Wu Y, de Groen PC, Natafgi N et al

cited_by.title: Colonoscopy: when to start and how often

record.population: 28,100 average-risk adults aged 40 to 89 at first screening colonoscopy in South Carolina, 58.4% Black
record.finding: Black patients had lower age- and sex-adjusted odds of an adenoma (odds ratio 0.88) than white patients, and similar odds of advanced adenoma or three or more non-advanced adenomas. The authors say polyp profiles were similar and that other factors must explain the higher bowel cancer rates in Black Americans.
record.note: Racially balanced sample, one US state; includes ages 40 to 49.
